rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thajjaj describes abundant water or liquid pouring and rushing, whether intransitively or as something poured.
rows.anchor: Suyun veya bir mâyi‘in kesretle dökülüp şarlayarak akması veya akıtılmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase explains the purpose or consequence of sending rain; lam marks consequence and bi marks causation.
rows.anchor: İnzâlin hikmetini ve gayesini beyandır. Lâm âkıbet, bâ sebebiyet içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alfaf is the plural of leff: interwoven, tangled, or embracing gardens.
rows.anchor: “Leff”in cem‘i, mültef, girift yani sarmaş dolaş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed Day of Decision concludes the signs just established: waking, harvest, and the end of worldly life, resolving disputes and accounting for blessings.
rows.anchor: bir had ve nihâyet olmak üzere ilm-i ilâhîde tâyin edilmiş bir mîkāt olduğu muhakkaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs should make people understand the day's coming, otherwise they will later know it with certainty; its time is fixed in divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: Bu delillerden icmâlen olsun anlamanız lâzım gelir, anlamak istemediğiniz surette de ileride kat‘iyyen bileceksiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision is certainly coming and is an unfailing appointment, as also stated in al-Mursalat.
rows.anchor: muhakkak bir fasıl günü gelecektir. Ve o şaşmaz bir mîkāttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet here is the second blast of resurrection and awakening, rather than the first blast of destruction.
rows.anchor: kıyam ve intibah nefhası olan nefha-i sâniye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is explanatory: the dead rise as from sleep and come to the gathering in successive groups.
rows.anchor: fâ fasîhadır. Yani Sûr üfürülünce siz ölüler uykudan uyanır gibi uyanır kalkarsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community is summoned with its imam and arrives in its own group, in accordance with the wording of al-Isra.
rows.anchor: her ümmet imamıyla çağırılarak derhâl alay alay, ümmet ümmet, cemaat cemaat mahşere gelirsiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's order changes and it opens into what seem to be doors, allowing the Spirit and angels to descend and stand in ranks.
rows.anchor: emr-i ilâhî ile melekler inecek, Rûh ve melâike saf saf olacaktır

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi equates the opening with the sky's splitting and breaking apart because these terms are near in meaning.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Bu fetih إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Razi's equation is not strong: opening doors differs from splitting, since the sky could open into doors while its substance remains unbroken.
rows.anchor: bu pek kavî değildir. Çünkü kapı açılmaktan anlaşılan mâna ‘teşakkuk’ ve ‘tefattur’dan anlaşılan mânadan başkadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this passage describes the resurrection blast, the opening follows the sky's total folding and destruction and begins the renewed afterlife order, fitting the following day of ranked spirits and angels.
rows.anchor: semânın tayyı ile fenâ-i küllîden sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These afterlife gates open for those entering Paradise but stay closed to disbelievers; this is the afterlife heaven, not the worldly sky that will split.
rows.anchor: kâfirler için açılmayıp cennete girecekler için açılacak olan semâ kapıları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains vanish like mirages after the first blast scattered and crushed them; the earth is leveled, and mountains can no longer shield it from upheaval.
rows.anchor: dağlar o gün serab gibi hayâle dönmüş, artık ıztırâbâta sed çekecek hiçbir hâlleri kalmamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirsad is chiefly a place of watching or ambush, like a hunter's lookout, though it can name the observing instrument or place; its intensive form can figuratively mean a place characterized by constant watching.
rows.anchor: rasad yeri, terassud mahalli mânasına kullanılır ki avcının av gözlediği yer gibi gözetme yeri

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says relational predicates imply abundance and permanence: Hell is where angels watch to seize rebels whose punishment is decreed.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân der ki: “Nisbet mânasına delâlet eden haberlerin ve sıfatların hepsinde teksir ve lüzum mânası vardır

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses Hell as the prison of enemies and the passageway of friends.
rows.anchor: Mukātil demiştir ki düşmanların mahbisi, dostların geçiti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-t-taghin can attach to mirsad, making Hell a lookout for rebels, or to ma'ab, making it the rebels' final place of return.
rows.anchor: tuğyan edenler, azgınlık yapanlar için ki bu, “mirsâd”a da, “meâb”a da ta‘alluk edebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labithin means remaining residents and is an anticipated state of the transgressors; ahqaba is the plural of huqub, an era containing successive years.
rows.anchor: mânasına “tâğīn”den hâl-i mukadderedir. Yani o hâlde ki onlar orada ikāmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huqub is commonly said to mean eighty-odd years; another transmitted reckoning makes it about twenty-nine thousand years using afterlife days, while some say seventy thousand years.
rows.anchor: seksen küsur yıl diye şâyi‘dir. Her biri bin sene demek olan âhiret günleriyle senesi üç yüz altmış gün olmak üzere seksen yıl diye mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer a finite duration from huqub, but exegetes also understand ahqaba as endlessly successive eras, and many gloss huqub as eternity.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn demişlerdir ki bu kelimede tetâbu‘ve tevâlî mefhûmu bulunduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A finite singular huqub does not entail a finite plural ahqaba; even if finitude were inferred, that implication cannot override explicit statements of eternity elsewhere.
rows.anchor: müfred olan “hukub”un mütenâhî olmasından cem‘i olan “ahkāb”ın da mütenâhî olması lâzım gelmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If transgressors includes sinful believers, a transmitted hadith says their reserved layer of Hell eventually goes out; this would limit punishment only for that group.
rows.anchor: cehennemin usât-ı mü’minîne mahsus olan tabakası nihâyet söneceği hakkında bir hadîs-i şerif de mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description may also allude to the condition of peoples conquered and held captive in this world.
rows.anchor: dünyada mahkum ve esir milletlerin hâllerine de bir işaret çıkarılabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bard means cool air or sleep; hamim is boiling water, and ghassaaq is flowing pus from Hell's people, from a root meaning to pour or flow.
rows.anchor: “Hamîm” sıcak kaynar su, “Gassâk” ehl-i cehennemin cesedlerinden dökülen akan irin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wifaq is an emphatic verbal noun used adjectivally for a fully fitting recompense, since their denial was absolute; kadhdhabu is a verbal noun from form II meaning denial.
rows.anchor: Vech-i muvafakat, çünkü tekzib ebedî nefiydir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to increase them only in punishment explicitly establishes punishment's unending duration.
rows.anchor: Bu da azâbın ‘adem-i tenâhîsinde nastır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the transgressors and deniers, the passage turns to the condition of the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: Tâğīlerin, mükezziblerin hâlini beyandan sonra müttakīlerin hâline geçilerek buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamma comes from a root meaning to overwhelm or fill; the greatest catastrophe names the resurrection, especially when Hell's and Paradise's people enter their destinations.
rows.anchor: “Tâmme” basıp doldurmak mânasına طَمَّ’den müştak olarak üstün ve baskın güç yetmez belâ demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembrance of what a person strove for is appositional to the greatest catastrophe: then each recognizes the aims and good or evil pursued, and profit or loss incurred.
rows.anchor: “Tâmme-i kübrâ”dan bedeldir. Yani o tâmme-i kübrâ, o gün ki insan neye çalışmış olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is made conspicuous when its gates open and its flames burst forth; a transmitted report says everyone with sight will see it.
rows.anchor: Çünkü rivayet olunduğuna göre cehennem açılacak, alevler saçarak fırlayacak, her gözü olan görecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone reaches Hell and Paradise's people cross the bridge over it; those who see may mean all capable of sight or specifically entering disbelievers and rebels.
rows.anchor: herkes ona varacak, ehl-i cennet de sırâtı onun üzerinden geçecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase for those who see can also specifically mean those who enter Hell, the disbelievers and transgressors.
rows.anchor: “görecek kimseler için” demek, girecek kâfirler ve azgınlar için demek de olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's standing-place is the servant's presence before God at the catastrophe when the Spirit and angels stand in ranks, or the place where the servant will stand.
rows.anchor: kulun huzûr-i ilâhîde duruşu veya duracağı makamdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mursa is a verbal noun of bringing something to rest, or a place or time meaning endpoint; like a ship anchored, the question asks when God will bring the Hour to pass.
rows.anchor: Burada bir istiare var demek olur. Yani Allah o Sâ‘at’i ne vakit getirip dikecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading rejects the question: the Prophet has no task of specifying the Hour and its timing lies beyond him.
rows.anchor: nerdesin sen onu anlatmaktan? Onu anlatmak senin vazifen değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading treats the question as misplaced and the Prophet's mission as itself a sign that the Hour is approaching; seeking further details exceeds their authority.
rows.anchor: sen Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ onun alâmetlerindensin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the Hour's full reality and all its details for everyone until it occurs; the Prophet is not charged to reveal more.
rows.anchor: Bütün künhüyle ve herkes hakkında vukū‘u vaktine kadar bütün tafsîlâtıyla onu bilmek Rabbine aittir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a warner for those who fear the Hour and will guard themselves.
rows.anchor: sen ancak ondan haşyet duyacak, korunacak olan kimseleri sakındıracak habercisin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Hour, worldly life will seem no longer than an evening or its forenoon; life passes quickly, the cautious escape its terrors, and the heedless reach everlasting calamity.
rows.anchor: Uzun zannedilen dünya ömrü o kadar çabuk geçer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because warning benefits those who fear, later suras will continue to explain whom these warnings benefit and how.
rows.anchor: bu inzârlar, âtîdeki sûrelerde de tevâlî ettirilerek anlatılacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind seeker may purify himself fully, or learn gradually and benefit from the reminder by recognizing good and evil and acting accordingly; the first is completion, the second progress toward it.
rows.anchor: Ya günah âsârından bir şey kalmayacak vechile tamamen tezekkî ve tefeyyüz, yahut tezekkür ede ede ileride intifâ‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker came asking for guidance and Quran, with either complete purification or gradual benefit reasonably hoped for; the Prophet did not know this when he turned away.
rows.anchor: Onun o a‘mâ hâlinde gelerek “yâ Resûlallah beni irşad et, bana Kur’an oku” demesinde bu iki ihtimalden biri melhuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-sufficient person may consider himself above faith, advice, and learning, or may be wealthy; the Prophet instead devotes attention to him.
rows.anchor: imandan, öğütten, tezekkür ve tezekkîden istiğnâ eden, kendisini ihtiyaçsız sayıp da senden ders almak istemeyen veya zengin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports Bahr's first derivation of tasadda from sadad: the Prophet attends to the man and works for his guidance and reform.
rows.anchor: “Tesaddâ” “saded”den, yahut “sadâ”dan olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahr's alternative derives tasadda from sada: the Prophet waits eagerly for the man's response, like expecting an echo from distant mountains.
rows.anchor: “sen ondan sadâ bekliyor, uzaktan uzağa, dağdan taştan ses in‘ikâsını beklemek gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet bears no responsibility if the self-sufficient person refuses purification or Islam, but ignoring a Muslim who seeks instruction entails responsibility; guidance efforts toward unbelievers remain permissible in principle.
rows.anchor: müstağnînin temizlenmemesinden, İslâm’a girmemesinden sana bir mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind poor seeker came eagerly for knowledge and guidance, fearing sin and showing reverence, yet the Prophet ignored him for an unproductive effort with the self-sufficient man.
rows.anchor: bir kusur eder sürçerim, bir günaha girerim diye Allah korkusu, Hak saygısı ile gelen kimse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though outwardly blind, the seeker has an open ear and heart, unlike the sighted self-sufficient person whose inner eye is blind and who will not hear truth.
rows.anchor: zâhir gözü görmezse de kulağı ve kalb gözü açık hidâyet âşığı bir tâlibi bırakıyorsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasadda and talahha are second-person present verbs, shortened from tataṣadda and tatalahha.
rows.anchor: تَصَدَّىٰ ve تَلَهَّىٰ fiilleri mâzî değil, muzâri‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla forbids this behavior: the Quran is a reminder that recalls God, duty, and good; the wish-to-remember clause functions as warning and threat rather than neutral permission.
rows.anchor: bu suretle meşiyyete ta‘lîk tahyir için değil, Türkçemizde de meselâ “canı isteyen dinlesin” dediğimiz zaman kasdettiğimiz mâna gibi bir inzar ve tehdid mâhiyetindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhkira is both the act of reminding and an object that helps one remember, such as a thread on a finger, an instructive saying, notebook, book, letter, or written work.
rows.anchor: parmağa bağlanan bir iplik, unutulmayıp kulakta küpe olacak ibretli bir söz, bir muhtıra defteri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding primarily recalls something known but neglected, while it can also impart something new; the whole Quran, its verses, pages, and suras are God's reminder.
rows.anchor: Kur’an; âyetleri, sahîfeleri, sûreleri ve hey’et-i mecmû‘ası ile de taraf-ı ilâhîden bir tezkiredir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhuf are sheets of writing, broadly pages or leaves, and by extension letters, epistles, books, or scriptures; a bound collection is a mushaf.
rows.anchor: “sahîfe” yazılı veya yazılacak kâğıttan, kırtastan bir parçadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was memorized and written from its Meccan revelation on separate surfaces such as wood, leather, stone, bone, and leaves; Abu Bakr first gathered and bound it as one volume.
rows.anchor: Kur’an ta Mekke’de nüzûlünden itibaren hem ezberlenmeye hem yazılmaya başlamış olmakla beraber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here suhuf most readily means Quran pages, including the Preserved Tablet's pages, angelic copies from it, and sheets later assembled into the mushaf; reports about these are not exclusive alternatives.
rows.anchor: Levh-i Mahfûz’a yazdığı sahîfelere ve melâikenin Levh-i Mahfuz’dan istinsah edip vahiy ile getirdikleri sahîfelere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukarrama means honored by God and deserving reverence; marfu'a means exalted in status and literally to be kept high and above the waist when read.
rows.anchor: Onun için mushaflar yüksek, hürmetli yerlere konmalı ve okunurken belden yukarı tutulmalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutahhara means protected from physical and spiritual impurity, so Quran pages should be kept clean and touched only with clean, ritually pure hands.
rows.anchor: Kirli, taharetsiz eller sürülmez, tertemiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biaydi safara may be a further adjective describing the pages or may instead modify mutahhara.
rows.anchor: sıfat ba‘de sıfat olmak muhtemil olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safara is plural of safir, a writer or scribe, from sefr meaning writing; because writing uncovers meaning, the root can mean uncovering, and sefr means a book.
rows.anchor: “Sâfir”, “ketb” vezninde ve aynı mânada, yani yazı yazmak demek olan “sefr”den kâtib, kitap yazıcı, hattat mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safir could mean a cleaner or traveler/envoy, but the plural for travelers would be asfar or suffar rather than safara; an envoy can reconcile quarrels.
rows.anchor: Bir yerden bir yere gitmek mânasına mâlum olan “sefer”den “sâfir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the pages, safara can mean writers, envoys who bring them, or custodians who sweep and keep books clean; exegetes most often identify them as angels.
rows.anchor: Ekseriyetle “ketebe” veya “süferâ” melâike mânasına tefsir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukhari transmits interpretations taking mutahhara as pages only the purified touch, identifying them as angels and comparing them to angels who direct affairs; both pages and carriers are purified.
rows.anchor: Ona ancak mutahhar olanlar messeder ve onlar melâikedir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses safara as writers who write books.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas da: سَفَرَةٍ، كَتَبَةٍ أَسْفَارًا: yani “kitapları yazan ketebe” demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These interpretations encompass angels writing the Preserved Tablet and copying scriptures, angels recording deeds, and possibly human scribes writing the mushaf.
rows.anchor: Levh-i Mahfûz’u yazan melâike ile Levh’ten kütüb-i ilâhiyeyi emrolunan mahallere tevdî‘etmek üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes mainly derive safara from writing or envoy work: many specify angels, some prophets, and one report from Qatada generalizes it to Quran people; restricting it to all prophets seems remote here.
rows.anchor: çokları melâikeye bazıları enbiyâya tahsis etmiş, Katâde’den bir rivayette de ehl-i Kur’an diye ta‘mîm edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, safara encompasses those serving Quran's revelation, preservation, writing, understanding, and teaching; the root can include envoys, scribes, custodians, explainers, and readers.
rows.anchor: hâmiller murad olunmak iktizâ eder. Ve “sefere” maddesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These safara are further described as noble and obedient.
rows.anchor: ki bu sefere {كِرَامٍۭ بَرَرَةٍۢ} “kirâm-ı berere” sıfatlarıyla tavsif edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kiram derives from honoring or generosity: the angels are either revered by God or compassionate toward believers, praying for their forgiveness.
rows.anchor: Tekrim ve tevkīr mânasına “kerâmet”ten olduğuna göre Allah teâlâ indinde muazzez ve muvakkarlar demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barara can mean those abundant in good or truthful in word and deed; both senses together yield the pious and God-fearing.
rows.anchor: kavillerinde ve fiillerinde sâdık demek olur ki ikisine de şâmil olmak üzere ehl-i takvâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes distinguish ebrar for humans, whose pious are few, from barara for angels, whose multitude are all obedient and pious.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da “ebrâr” Benî Âdem’den olanlar hakkında, “berere” de melâike hakkında vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar expression safarat al-kiram al-barara chiefly denotes angels, while by implication it can describe people sharing those qualities.
rows.anchor: lisân-ı şer‘de “sefere-i kirâm-ı berere” melâike olmak üzere mâruftur

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: Aisha transmits the Prophet's saying that a memorizing Quran reciter is with the noble obedient envoys, while one who struggles but persists receives two rewards.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den şu hadîs-i şerîf rivayet edilmiştir: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurdu ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a reminder in honored, elevated, purified pages held by noble obedient envoys; whoever wishes should reflect, remember, and act.
rows.anchor: o Kur’an böyle kirâm-ı berere-i sefere ellerinde öyle mutahhar, merfû‘, mükerrem sahîfeler içinde bir tezkiredir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding awakens thought and attention, moving from the known toward the unknown; the Quran recalls familiar signs in human nature to awaken faith, worship, and preparation for the afterlife without obscure proofs.
rows.anchor: insana Allah’ın sun‘u kudretiyle âhiretin hevl ü dehşetini duyurmak ve O’na karşı vazife ve ubûdiyet hissini tehyic ederek iman ve islâm ile tezekkî ve terakki şevkini uyandırmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutil al-insan is a curse and rebuke, like saying may the person be ruined; it condemns a condition so vile that he scarcely deserves life.
rows.anchor: “kutile” Türkçemizde “kahrolası” tâbiri gibi gazab ve zemme delâlet eyleyen beddua suretinde takbihten kinayedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation about ingratitude states the reason for the rebuke: people forget their origin, gifts from the benefactor, and God's power despite reminders.
rows.anchor: vücûdunun mebde’inden me‘âdı saatine kadar müstağrak olduğu nimeti unutmak ve mün‘imden ve onun kudretinden zühûl etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates the human from a drop and develops the embryo through many stages until it reaches a beautiful form.
rows.anchor: rüşeym hâlinden doğumuna kadar nice etvârdan geçirerek en güzel biçime koydu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the path easy includes the stages from birth until a person's intellect and reasoning mature.
rows.anchor: doğumundan akl u fikrinin tekemmülüne kadar geçirdiği merâtibe şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death and commands burial rather than leaving the body exposed, honoring both the living and the dead as a blessing.
rows.anchor: kabre defnedilmesini de emretti. İnsanın dirisini de, ölüsünü de muhterem kıldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will raise the dead after burial whenever He wills; the time of resurrection is not specified.
rows.anchor: Ölümünden sonra da o kabirde öyle bırakacak değildir. Dilediği zaman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators take kalla here to mean indeed or truly.
rows.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğu burada “kellâ” hakkā mânasına olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: A report from Mujahid and Qatada says what humanity has not fulfilled is everything God commanded, from the beginning of obligation until burial, or from Adam's creation through the present.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ve Katâde’den nakledildiğine göre müfessirîn demişlerdir ki burada مَآ أَمَرَهُۥ’dan murad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qada implies completion and lamma comprehensive negation, so humanity has not fully discharged its obligation, gratitude, and servitude; grateful servants are few.
rows.anchor: “Kazâ”da itmam mânası bulunduğu ve لَمَّا cahd-ı müstağrak ifade eylediği cihetle nefy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to humanity as a species or the self-satisfied person, not every individual; this does not exclude the purified few who fulfill their duties.
rows.anchor: ibâd-ı muhlasîn gibi bazı ferdlerin vazifelerini îfâ etmiş olmalarına mâni‘olmazsa da cins-i beşerin vazifesini tamamıyla hiç de yapmamış olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity still needs growth toward its intended perfection, as expressed by nabtalihi in Surat al-Insan; Abu Bakr lamented that it were complete.
rows.anchor: bu mâna Sûre-i İnsan’da نَبْتَل۪يهِ [76/2] kaydıyla ifade edilmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should examine their food and its gradual growth to recognize inner and outer blessings, give thanks, and use them rightly.
rows.anchor: nasıl bir kudret ve hikmet ile peyderpey terakki ederek yetiştirildiğine nazar etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water is the first material cause of food and life on earth; God creates and pours down the rain as a favor.
rows.anchor: o suyu Biz bir döküş dökmekteyiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain makes dry, lifeless earth stir and swell before it cracks and produces plants, a marvel attributed to God.
rows.anchor: yağmurlar nüzûlüyle ihtizâza gelip feyizlenmeye, sonra çatlayıp nebâtât çıkarmaya başlayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list includes grain, grapes, fresh greens, olives, dates, dense orchards, fruits, and pasture; human cultivation helps, but God gives the soil its power to grow them.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın sürülüşünde hubûbâtın ve bağların tımarında insanların mesâîlerinin de bir kıymeti olmakla beraber o kara toprakta böyle dâneler, üzümler yetiştirecek derecede feyz ü tekâmül uyandıran hep Allah teâlâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadb means fresh alfalfa or greens; ghulb describes thick-trunked, tall trees or gardens whose trees intertwine; fakiha includes fresh and dried fruit.
rows.anchor: “galbâ”nın cem‘i ki “hadîka-i galbâ” ağaçları iri, boylu ve birbirine girift bahçe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abb is explained as pasture, grass, vegetables, fodder, or provisions; its root means preparing and provisioning, with hay and dried foods also suggested.
rows.anchor: “ebb” ki çayır ve otlak, sebze, alef, çerez mânalarına geldiği söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root means preparation and provisioning, extended to pasture because it is cut or grazed for summer and winter; hay and dried foods are also suggested.
rows.anchor: bu kelime esasen hazırlanmak, tedarükâtta bulunmak mânasına mevzû‘olup yaz ve kış için biçmeye ve hayvan gütmeye elverişli olması itibariyle ota ve otlağa ıtlâkı

rows.speaker: Ebû Bekir
rows.claim: Asked what abb means, Abu Bakr refused to speak about God's Book without knowledge, asking what sky would shade or earth would shelter him if he did.
rows.anchor: Ebû Bekir Sıddîk radıyallahu anh’tan “‘ebb’ nedir?” diye sorulduğunda “beni hangi semâ gölgelendirir ve hangi arz barındırır

rows.speaker: Ömer
rows.claim: Umar recited the listed crops and asked what abb meant; he broke his staff, called such speculation needless strain, and advised acting on what is clear and leaving the unknown to God.
rows.anchor: “Hayât-ı ilâhiyeye kasem ederim ki bu tekellüftür. Ey Ömer’in anasının oğlu, ‘ebben’ ne olduğunu bilmesen ne var?

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: The Kashshaf says Umar did not forbid study of Quranic meanings; he prioritized action, since the passage calls for gratitude and abb is generally known to be useful vegetation.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf demiştir ki: “Hazret-i Ömer’in bu sözünde

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: A believer should not waste time identifying the exact species named abb; give thanks for understood blessings and await clarification while keeping the general sense.
rows.anchor: Burada mü’mine asıl ehem olan vecîbe has ismi ‘ebb’ olan otların ne olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran includes difficult or general words whose full meanings may not be grasped immediately; believers may accept a general sense until later clarification.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da herkesin her zaman mânasını ihâta edemeyeceği ve ancak mücmel bir mefhum ile iktifâ olunarak iman edilmesi lâzım gelen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abb summarizes many fresh and dry plants useful to people and animals, like mar'a in the previous sura; its full scope would require lengthy inquiry.
rows.anchor: evvelki sûredeki “mer‘âhâ” mânasına olmakla beraber daha neler neler gibi insan ve hayvânâtın intifâ‘edebileceği yaş ve kuru birçok nebâtâta şâmil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because abb's root conveys preparation and readiness, the list may hint that the afterlife also requires many preparations and provisions.
rows.anchor: bu kelimenin asl-ı vaz‘ında hazırlık, isti‘dad ve teheyyü’ mânası bulunması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakhkha, like tamma, names a grave calamity and specifically the second or final blast of resurrection.
rows.anchor: “sâhha”, “tâmme” gibi büyük belâ ve dâhiye mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sakhh describes striking a hard, solid object forcefully against another; sakhkha can name the impact or sound it produces.
rows.anchor: “Sahh” demir ve taş gibi katı ve pek bir şeyi içi boş olmayan yine öyle dolgun bir şeye çarpmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By metonymy, sakhkha is the forceful cry that strikes and deafens ears, then the overwhelming calamity named for that cry.
rows.anchor: Bundan isnâd-ı mecâzî suretiyle “sâhha” çarpınca kulağı sağır eden şiddetli sayhaya da ıtlak olunur
